item.title: DOJ misconduct complaint against D.C. federal judge dismissed
item.description: A federal appeals court dismissed a judicial misconduct complaint against D.C. Judge James Boasberg, finding no evidence of bias against Trump.

item.title: Judge in Charlie Kirk case to consider bid to disqualify prosecutors
item.description: Lawyers for the man accused of killing Charlie Kirk ask a judge to dismiss prosecutors over alleged conflict of interest because the lead prosecutor’s daughter witnessed the killing.

item.title: Fundraising gap widens in Wisconsin Supreme Court race
item.description: New filings show liberal candidate Chris Taylor vastly outpacing conservative rival Maria Lazar in fundraising ahead of Wisconsin’s April Supreme Court election.

item.title: 10th Circuit faults Kansas troopers but narrows car search injunction
item.description: A federal appeals court ruled Kansas Highway Patrol violated drivers’ Fourth Amendment rights but cut back a lower court’s sweeping injunction.

item.title: ICE demands cooperation. What does state already do?
item.description: Minnesota officials say they already cooperate with ICE as required by law, citing constitutional limits on detainer requests and jail access.

item.title: Trial lawyer Rich Ruohonen heads to Winter Olympics
item.description: TSR Injury Law partner Rich Ruohonen will compete in Olympic curling after decades of courtroom and ice victories.

item.title: Carlo Faccini named partner at Heimerl & Lammers
item.description: Carlo Faccini has been promoted to partner at Heimerl & Lammers in recognition of his leadership within the firm, his dedication to clients across Minnesota, and his statewide impact on family law practice.

item.title: Trump to pull 700 immigration agents from Minnesota
item.description: The Trump administration will withdraw 700 immigration agents from Minnesota, though about 2,000 remain amid lawsuits, protests, and shootings.

item.title: Minnesota teachers sue to keep ICE off school property
item.description: Minnesota school districts and educators sued DHS, alleging immigration enforcement near schools has hurt attendance and disrupted learning statewide.

item.title: 8th Circuit upholds conviction in Red Lake child neglect case
item.description: The 8th Circuit affirmed a felony child neglect conviction under the Major Crimes Act after a child died of malnutrition on the Red Lake Reservation.
